answer: A verifiable delay protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to anchor its identity to an unparallelizable sequential computation. An attacker cannot multiplex identities, as each agent requires a dedicated execution core run at its frequency zenith. Rather than running cheap virtual clones across a server tundra, adversaries incur linear hardware and electricity costs. However, this design causes continuous energy waste and favors entities with custom ASICs.
